children: KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--Malaysia Aviation Group has ordered 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft, with options for six more, marking the latest in a string of order wins in Asia for the U.S. planemaker.

The aircraft, powered by GE Aerospace engines, are scheduled for delivery between 2032 and 2035, the parent company of Malaysia Airlines said Wednesday. The order is part of MAG's efforts to modernize its long-haul fleet.

Malaysia Airlines will become the first Malaysian carrier to operate the Boeing 787. The 787 Dreamliners are expected to serve routes including London, Paris, Sydney, Melbourne, Tokyo, Osaka and Seoul.
The new aircraft will gradually replace MAG's seven Airbus A350, which are expected to be phased out between 2032 and 2035.

Malaysia Airlines currently operates more than 37 next-generation Boeing 737 aircraft and 19 Boeing 737-8s. The airline also renewed its agreement with GE Aerospace for fuel-management and flight-efficiency software.
The Boeing order comes amid a series of U.S. aviation deals in Asia following President Donald Trump's recent visit to the region.
Xiamen Airlines agreed to buy 50 Boeing 737-8 jets valued at $7.4 billion, while Boeing and GE Aerospace finalized a $12 billion deal to supply Philippine Airlines with up to 20 Boeing 787 aircraft.
